newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Jan 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Jan 24.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The inflation rate this year could reach 7.9 percent provided that there will be no further negative developments. According to the governer of the Czech National Bank (CNB), Josef Tosovsky, the CNB is doing all possible to ensure that rather bad tendencies do not increase the risk of harming the economy.

- Finance Minister and Vice-chairman of the Cabinet, Ivan Kocarnik, will continue discussions in Moscow today with Russian deputy prime minister, Vladimir Babichev, pertaining to trade and scientific-technical cooperation between the Czech Republic and Russia.

- Banka Hana could get up to 3.3 billion crowns from the Czech National Bank, which is providing rehabilitation programmes for small monetary institutions, provided shareholders go through with their plan to increase the bank's capital to three billion crowns. The plan was approved in a shareholders' meeting yesterday.

PRAVO - According to the head of the school workers union, Jaroslav Rossler, if the strike for an increase in teachers' salaries is not successful, much harsher methods will be used. The chain strike, during which schools, youth centres and cafeterias will be closed, will begin in Brno and the districts of Znojmo, Blansko and Nachod on January 28.

- Chairman of Parliament and the Social Democratic Party (CSSD) Milos Zeman was not pleased with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's announcement that after the signing of the Czech-German Declaration, property claims of the Sudeten Germans will remain open.

LIDOVE NOVINY - A proposal for a new water law became the first law in history yesterday to be modified and returned to parliament by the senate for further discussions. The new version calls for a smaller safety zone around water sources.

- According to European Commissioner Hans van den Broek, privatisation of the bank sector, restructuring of businesses, clarification and fast introduction of compatible legislature are the main tasks which the Czech Republic must perform before obtaining membership in the EU.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - After it was brought to light that doctors at General Faculty Hospital in Prague, the largest health facility in the country, have had a shortage of certain necessary medicines in the past few days due to a lack of funds, opinions are being voiced that a similar situation could occur in other hospitals.
- Television stations sold a total of 5.58 billion crowns worth of air time for advertising last year, overtaking newspapers and magazines, which took in 4.8 billion crowns total.
